# CLI reference

Every command the `memini` binary accepts. Running `memini` with no arguments starts
the server; everything else is an operational subcommand.

The server is configured entirely through the environment rather than flags, so the
flags below belong to the subcommands only. See the
[configuration reference](configuration.md) for the environment.

## Commands

| Command | Does |
| --- | --- |
| [`memini backfill`](#memini-backfill) | Seed nil confidence on legacy durable memories (pre-0.0.11 recovery) |
| [`memini doctor`](#memini-doctor) | Diagnose namespace mismatches and store health |
| [`memini export`](#memini-export) | Export memories to memini's portable JSON (re-importable for backup/migration) |
| [`memini forget`](#memini-forget) | Bulk-delete memories by tag (e.g. undo a bad import) |
| [`memini import`](#memini-import) | Bulk-load an export from another memory system |
| [`memini key`](#memini-key) | Manage local API keys (this store's api_keys table only) |
| [`memini key add`](#memini-key-add) | Create an API key, or rotate an existing one's secret |
| [`memini key ls`](#memini-key-ls) | List API keys (name, home/default namespace, created, disabled, admin, read-only — never secrets or hashes) |
| [`memini key rm`](#memini-key-rm) | Delete an API key |
| [`memini link`](#memini-link) | Manage cross-namespace read links (durable-tier recall from another namespace) |
| [`memini link add`](#memini-link-add) | Create or replace a read link from src to dst |
| [`memini link ls`](#memini-link-ls) | List read links (every link in the store when src is omitted) |
| [`memini link rm`](#memini-link-rm) | Remove a read link |
| [`memini mcp`](#memini-mcp) | Serve MCP tools over stdio |
| [`memini migrate`](#memini-migrate) | One-shot data migrations between memini scope models |
| [`memini migrate scopes`](#memini-migrate-scopes) | Merge &lt;tenant&gt;/_shared namespaces into &lt;tenant&gt; (old shared-scope model -&gt; ancestor cascade) |
| [`memini namespace`](#memini-namespace) | Inspect and repair memory namespaces (recovery from botched imports / shared pools) |
| [`memini namespace list`](#memini-namespace-list) | List namespaces and their memory counts |
| [`memini namespace move`](#memini-namespace-move) | Move every memory from one namespace to another |
| [`memini namespace split`](#memini-namespace-split) | Regroup a pooled namespace back into per-source namespaces by metadata |
| [`memini reembed`](#memini-reembed) | Re-embed every memory under the currently configured embedding model |
| [`memini version`](#memini-version) | Print version information |

## `memini backfill`

Walk every namespace and seed ConfidenceSeedImported on durable (semantic / procedural) memories written before the confidence field existed, so they enter the decay + demotion lifecycle. Idempotent.

```
memini backfill [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes` |  | apply the backfill (default is a dry-run report) |

## `memini doctor`

Report how the namespace resolves for writes vs recall, list per-namespace memory counts, and flag the conditions behind 'agents stopped writing' and 'all my memories merged into one pool'. Read-only unless --fix is given.

```
memini doctor [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--fix` |  | after diagnosing, remediate: split attributable pools, backfill legacy confidence, purge expired, scrub content junk, demote stale durable debris, dedup |
| `--scrub` |  | remove content-level junk only: session-lifecycle markers and exact-duplicate memories (preview unless --yes) |
| `--yes` |  | apply --fix/--scrub changes (without it, they only preview) |

## `memini export`

Export a namespace's memories to a JSON document re-importable with `memini import --source memini`. Writes stdout when no path or -o is given. Filter with --tier/--tag/--meta to export a slice.

```
memini export [file] [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--all-namespaces` |  | export every namespace (each record keeps its own namespace) |
| `--include-expired` |  | include memories past their TTL |
| `--include-superseded` |  | include contradiction-tombstoned memories |
| `--meta` |  | restrict to memories whose metadata contains each key=value pair (repeatable, AND) |
| `--namespace` |  | namespace to export (defaults to the resolved default) |
| `--output` |  | write to this file instead of stdout |
| `--pretty` |  | indent the JSON output |
| `--tag` |  | restrict to memories carrying every listed tag (repeatable, AND) |
| `--tier` |  | restrict to these tiers (repeatable; working\|episodic\|semantic\|procedural) |

## `memini forget`

Delete every memory in a namespace carrying the given tag. The import command stamps each record with import:&lt;source&gt;:&lt;date&gt;, so a single `memini forget --tag import:mem0:2026-06-12` undoes that import.

```
memini forget [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--namespace` |  | namespace to delete from (defaults to the resolved default) |
| `--tag` |  | delete memories carrying this exact tag (required) |

## `memini import`

Bulk-load an export from another memory system (or memini's own format) into the local store or a remote server (--remote). Reads stdin when the path is "-" or omitted.

```
memini import [file] [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--batch` | `0` | records per batch (0 = backend default) |
| `--confidence` | `-1` | seed confidence for durable imported facts (0..1); &lt;0 uses the default low import seed so they earn trust on recall |
| `--dedup-similarity` | `0.85` | similarity threshold for the post-import dedup pass |
| `--dry-run` |  | parse and report where records would land without writing anything |
| `--extract` |  | also distil decisions/preferences/problems from conversations into durable semantic memories (no LLM) |
| `--importance` | `0.25` | importance assigned to records whose source carried none, so bulk imports rank below curated memories (0 = leave at 0) |
| `--merge-into` |  | force every record into this one namespace, discarding source namespaces (the original is kept in metadata for `namespace split`) |
| `--min-importance` | `0` | skip records below this importance (0 = off; note: sources without importance report 0) |
| `--min-length` | `20` | skip records whose trimmed content is shorter than this many bytes (0 = off) |
| `--namespace` |  | namespace for records whose source carried none (fallback only; does not override source namespaces) |
| `--no-dedup` |  | skip dedup of imported records: both the write-time exact-content skip and the post-import vector-cluster pass |
| `--remote` |  | target a running memini server (e.g. https://memini.example.com) instead of the local store |
| `--source` | `memini` | export format: agentmemory\|claude-code\|mem0\|memini\|mnemory |
| `--token` |  | bearer token for the remote server (defaults to MEMINI_API_KEY) |
| `--yes` |  | skip the confirmation prompt when --merge-into collapses multiple source namespaces |

## `memini key`

Manage API keys persisted in this store's api_keys table. This is unrelated to MEMINI_API_KEYS_FILE, a server-boot concept: keys declared there are loaded once when the server starts and cannot be created, rotated, or removed by this command.

```
memini key
```

## `memini key add`

Create a new named API key, generating a random secret that is printed exactly once to stdout — it is never stored and cannot be recovered or shown again, so save it now. Re-running with a name that already exists ROTATES that key: a new secret is generated and the old one stops authenticating immediately, while the key's CreatedAt, home/default namespace bindings, disabled state, admin state, and read-only state are all preserved unless the corresponding flag is explicitly passed (an explicit --home "" clears the binding; an explicit --disabled=false re-enables a disabled key — rotation alone never re-enables one; an explicit --admin=false demotes an admin key — rotation alone never demotes one; an explicit --read-only=false lifts the read-only restriction — rotation alone never lifts it).

```
memini key add <name> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--admin` |  | grant the key admin (the /v1/keys and /v1/settings/defaults surfaces, gated at the REST layer) |
| `--default-namespace` |  | namespace applied when a request presents this key with no explicit namespace header |
| `--disabled` |  | create the key already disabled |
| `--home` |  | bind the key to a home namespace (default: unbound) |
| `--read-only` |  | make the key read-only: it may read but every mutating request is refused, over both REST and MCP |

## `memini key ls`

List API keys (name, home/default namespace, created, disabled, admin, read-only — never secrets or hashes)

```
memini key ls
```

## `memini key rm`

Delete an API key

```
memini key rm <name>
```

## `memini link`

Manage cross-namespace read links (durable-tier recall from another namespace)

```
memini link
```

## `memini link add`

Create or replace a read link: recall scoped to src additionally reads durable (semantic/procedural) memories from dst. Re-running with the same src/dst replaces the tiers/note in place (upsert), never duplicates. dst need not exist yet — namespaces exist implicitly.

```
memini link add <src> <dst> [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--note` |  | free-text note explaining why the link exists |
| `--tiers` |  | comma-separated tiers this link admits, e.g. semantic,procedural (default: the service's durable default) |

## `memini link ls`

List read links (every link in the store when src is omitted)

```
memini link ls [src]
```

## `memini link rm`

Remove a read link

```
memini link rm <src> <dst>
```

Serve MCP tools over stdio

memini mcp
```

## `memini migrate`

One-shot data migrations between memini scope models

```
memini migrate
```

## `memini migrate scopes`

The old scope model merged a `<tenant>/_shared` namespace read-only into every sibling under &lt;tenant&gt; (and, separately, a MEMINI_GLOBAL_NAMESPACE merged into every namespace store-wide). The new model has interior namespaces AS the shared layer via the ancestor cascade, so this command folds the old data forward: every namespace literally named "&lt;prefix&gt;/_shared" is moved into "&lt;prefix&gt;" (link endpoints follow along), then a dedup pass runs against the target to collapse any facts the merge just duplicated. A bare "_shared" (no prefix) has no parent to merge into and is left alone, reported as a note. Idempotent: once no "&lt;prefix&gt;/_shared" namespace holds any memories, re-running finds nothing to do.

Defaults to a dry-run report; pass --yes to apply.

```
memini migrate scopes [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--yes` |  | apply the migration, including the post-merge dedup pass (default is a dry-run report) |

## `memini namespace move`

Move every memory from one namespace to another

```
memini namespace move [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dry-run` |  | report what would move without writing |
| `--from` |  | source namespace (required) |
| `--to` |  | destination namespace (required) |

## `memini namespace split`

Regroup a namespace by metadata, moving each memory to the namespace named by the first grouping key it carries (default: import_source_namespace, user_id, agent_id, run_id, project). Memories with no grouping key stay put. This recovers a store whose imports collapsed into one pool.

```
memini namespace split [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--by` |  | comma-separated metadata keys to group by (default: import_source_namespace,user_id,agent_id,run_id,project) |
| `--dry-run` |  | report the split without writing |
| `--from` |  | namespace to split (required) |

## `memini reembed`

Recompute and rewrite the vector for every stored memory using the model named by MEMINI_EMBED_MODEL, so the store can switch embedding models without being rebuilt from an export. Dimensionality cannot change here (the store is fixed at its original width); to change dims, create a new store and re-import. On success the store's recorded embedding model is updated so the startup guard accepts the new model.

```
memini reembed [flags]
```

| Flag | Default | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--batch` | `0` | memories embedded per request (0 = default) |
| `--namespace` |  | limit to a single namespace (default: every namespace) |
| `--yes` |  | apply the re-embedding (default is a dry-run report) |

## `memini version`

Print version information

memini version
```
